evidence.title: Kiro docs: Set up Kiro for VS Code
evidence.finding: Kiro for VS Code installs from the Visual Studio Marketplace or Open VSX, is included in every plan and uses the same Kiro agent and .kiro folder.

evidence.title: Kiro docs: Agent notifications
evidence.finding: The IDE sends native OS notifications for agent execution events.

evidence.title: Kiro docs: Proactive usage notifications
evidence.finding: Kiro sends a low-resource notification at 80% of monthly credit usage with upgrade or add-on options; billing notifications are on by default.

evidence.title: Kiro docs: Authentication
evidence.finding: Sign-in uses GitHub, Google, AWS Builder ID, IAM Identity Center or an external identity provider on every surface.

evidence.title: Kiro docs: Agent Client Protocol
evidence.finding: Kiro IDE, CLI, Web and Mobile use ACP to reach the unified harness; ACP-compatible editors such as JetBrains IDEs and Zed connect through ACP with capabilities their client implements.

evidence.title: Kiro docs: How Kiro works
evidence.locator: One harness, many surfaces; tool checks; configuration table
evidence.finding: Every surface is a front end speaking ACP to a standalone harness process that runs locally or in a cloud sandbox. Every tool call is checked against permission rules and kiroignore patterns that keep files out of agent access.

evidence.title: Kiro docs: CLI headless mode
evidence.locator: Intro; API key requirements; tool trust
evidence.finding: kiro-cli runs non-interactively in CI with a KIRO_API_KEY; API keys are available only to Pro, Pro+, Pro Max and Power subscribers and admins must enable them for managed subscriptions; governance rules apply to headless sessions.

evidence.title: Kiro docs: Enterprise Management API
evidence.finding: 16 operations create, edit, publish and assign Kiro policies via SigV4; Enterprise Management is in preview in us-east-1 and eu-central-1 and the APIs are not yet publicly released (custom AWS CLI model).

evidence.title: Kiro docs: Custom agents
evidence.finding: Custom agent configuration files set which tools, permissions and context an agent has.

evidence.title: Kiro docs: Sub-agents
evidence.finding: The main agent spawns custom agents as sub-agents with isolated context, in parallel, and aggregates results.

evidence.title: Kiro docs: Agent Skills
evidence.finding: Skills are portable instruction packages following the open Agent Skills standard.

evidence.title: Kiro docs: Steering
evidence.finding: Markdown steering files in .kiro/steering give persistent project knowledge on IDE, CLI, Web and Mobile.

evidence.title: Kiro docs: Governance
evidence.finding: Administrators can disable MCP or restrict it to an allow-listed MCP registry at organization or account level.

evidence.title: Kiro docs: MCP
evidence.finding: MCP servers extend Kiro across all surfaces; server prompts and resources work on IDE, CLI and Web.

evidence.title: Kiro docs: Permissions
evidence.locator: Capability table; capabilities and effects; Approve for me in Kiro Web
evidence.finding: Capability rules (fs_read, fs_write, shell, web_fetch, mcp, subagent and others) with deny, ask, allow or evaluate effects and glob match patterns apply in IDE and CLI; Web approves every sandbox action by default. With Approve for me on Web, approved tool calls are marked Approved for you and blocked ones fail with a reason.

evidence.title: Kiro docs: Powers
evidence.finding: Powers package tools, workflows and best practices that Kiro activates on demand.

evidence.title: Kiro docs: Crew agent backends
evidence.finding: Crew sessions can run on Kiro CLI, Kiro Agent, Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Pi, goose or DeepSeek Harness backends; backends other than Kiro CLI are Experimental (Crew 0.10.0+).

evidence.title: Kiro docs: Schedule (Kiro Web)
evidence.locator: Intro; View your scheduled tasks; status and Edit
evidence.finding: Scheduled tasks run a prompt against GitHub or GitLab repositories on a schedule in autonomous mode without starting a session (Pro plans and up); they can be disabled, re-enabled and edited.

evidence.title: Kiro docs: Hook types
evidence.finding: Hooks trigger on file, task, prompt-submit, agent-stop, session-start and tool-use events; file and task triggers run in IDE and CLI V3, Web runs the prompt, stop, session and tool triggers.

evidence.title: Kiro docs: Crew quick start
evidence.finding: Crew is an open-source personal agent that runs on the user's machine, a local container or a remote machine they control, with its gateway at localhost:5476; first launch installs kiro-cli and signs in.

evidence.title: Kiro docs: Crew multi-instance
evidence.finding: Crew can run chats on remote hosts, EC2, home servers or Fargate over SSH or SSM from one dashboard; opt-in, off by default, behind a feature preview.

evidence.title: Kiro docs: Crew Slack
evidence.finding: DM the Crew agent from Slack; each DM thread is a session with streaming replies and approval buttons.

evidence.title: Kiro docs: Crew security
evidence.finding: Crew blocks protected credential paths, masks credential locations from subprocesses with its OS sandbox, redacts credential patterns and records every decision in a security event log.

evidence.title: Kiro docs: Crew Task Runner
evidence.finding: The Task Runner decomposes a spec into steps, tests each, retries and commits per step.

evidence.title: Kiro docs: Kiro Mobile
evidence.finding: Native app on Android (Google Play) and iPhone (TestFlight early access) for Pro-family plans; starts, follows and steers cloud sessions.

evidence.title: Kiro docs: Credit pooling
evidence.finding: One shared credit pool with no overages; seats $20/month add 500 credits; admins cap credits per user, with group and profile limits as fallbacks.

evidence.title: Kiro docs: Cancelling your subscription
evidence.finding: Cancelling means switching to Kiro Free; mid-month you keep the plan until month end and are not charged after.

evidence.title: Kiro docs: Export sessions
evidence.finding: Any IDE chat exports as a zip with prompts, responses, tool calls and code blocks.

evidence.title: Kiro docs: Deleting your account
evidence.finding: Deleting the account cancels subscriptions; it can be restored within 30 days, after which account and data are permanently deleted.

evidence.title: Kiro docs: Prompt logging
evidence.finding: Admins can log IDE and CLI prompts and responses to an S3 bucket in their own account.

evidence.title: Kiro docs: User activity
evidence.finding: Admins export per-user activity, including credit and overage use, as daily CSV to S3, daily OpenTelemetry metrics or real-time OpenTelemetry events.

evidence.title: Kiro docs: Data protection
evidence.locator: AWS regions where content is stored
evidence.finding: Free and individual subscriber content is stored in us-east-1; enterprise content may be stored in the profile's Region; inference location can differ.

evidence.title: Kiro docs: Compliance validation
evidence.finding: Kiro is in the scope of AWS's ISO/IEC 27001:2022 certification, verified by EY CertifyPoint; reports download through AWS Artifact, which requires Builder ID or IAM Identity Center sign-in.

evidence.title: Kiro docs: Enterprise support
evidence.finding: With an AWS Support plan including Kiro Enterprise support, cases go through AWS Support or the Kiro Support power.

evidence.title: Kiro CLI changelog 3.0.0
evidence.locator: V3 by Default, Classic and Desktop App Retired; Breaking changes
evidence.finding: CLI 3.0.0 (2026-11-03) made V3 default and retired the Classic interface, desktop app and inline autocomplete as breaking changes with migration notes; cloud sessions resume from /sessions.

evidence.title: Kiro docs: Kiro Web
evidence.finding: Kiro Web chats in a default collaborative mode, spec mode or autonomous mode and opens PRs or MRs; it never merges automatically.

evidence.title: Kiro docs: Autonomous mode
evidence.finding: Autonomous can be toggled before the first message or at any later point in the session.

evidence.title: Kiro docs: Sandbox
evidence.finding: Each task runs in its own isolated sandbox whose file state is kept with the session until the session is deleted.

evidence.title: Kiro docs: Sandbox internet access
evidence.finding: Network levels: connections only, common dependencies or open internet, plus a custom domain allow-list.

evidence.title: Kiro docs: Sandbox environment variables
evidence.finding: Environment variables and encrypted secrets are exposed to the sandbox; docs warn the agent may exfiltrate secrets.

evidence.title: Kiro docs: Sandbox environment configuration
evidence.finding: The Web agent detects the project type and configures the sandbox from manifests such as package.json or requirements.txt.

read.answer: Task Runner injects the spec, working memory and prior Git state into each step.

dependencies.answer: Task steps declare dependencies for parallel execution.

results.answer: Passed steps create Git commits; reviewer sessions inspect actual diffs.

approvals.answer: The Requirements-First workflow requests user confirmation before advancing phases.

worktree.answer: Existing repositories get a separate Git worktree per task run.

container.answer: Crew documents a Docker container runtime with its own persistent volumes and optional inner sandbox.

worker_crash.answer: Task Runner reconciles interrupted steps after a Gateway restart.

duplicate_actions.answer: Runs without Git/idempotency safeguards reopen paused with an unknown-side-effect notice.

manual_repair.answer: Humans inspect external state before resuming unsafe interrupted runs.

time_limits.answer: kirocrew run --timeout sets a run timeout.

retries.answer: Each step allows three logic/test retries, two crash recoveries and two replans.

enforcement.answer: The runner caps total tasks including replans at fifty and detects repeated-error loops.

concurrency.answer: Crew allows three concurrent task runs and parallel batches of three independent steps.

queues.answer: The shared scheduling queue is persisted in tasks.db.

cancellation.answer: CLI or dashboard can cancel a specific task or all tasks.

recovery.answer: Interrupted steps are reconciled against the Gateway incarnation and retry safety.

sso.answer: Organization sign-in supports IAM Identity Center or external IdP such as Okta and Microsoft Entra.

plan_scope.answer: Organization-managed access uses its admin-provided start URL/region or external identity-provider flow.

delivery.answer: Spec force_approval gates can protect deployment/publish steps.

allow.answer: The task pauses and shows Approve/Deny controls before a forced-approval step.

deny.answer: A forced approval gate can be denied in the dashboard.

tests.answer: Task steps run tests before committing unless --no-test is selected.

independent_review.answer: A separate reviewer session checks the actual Git diff.

configured_policy.answer: force_approval gates and --no-test configure distinct run behaviors.

retained_evidence.answer: Per-step commits and Git log/diff state feed later step prompts.
